requirements: R1: Task plans and definition of done must explicitly cover error states such as 400, 401, and 403.
R2: Pipeline audit and coverage checks must reflect actual implementation of Moodle role sync and the 401 API fix without mocking success.
R3: The backend must implement valid JWT verification and Moodle role synchronization rather than only optimistic locking exception handling.
R4: The authentication endpoint must accept valid credentials and return a documented 200/201 status rather than a 401.

slices.title: Fix authentication API to resolve 401 errors, JWT verification, and Moodle role sync
slices.jtbd: When implementing the resolution for this epic, I want to repair JWT verification and Moodle role sync in the backend, so that the self-falsification findings are addressed and users can authenticate successfully.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid credential, When authenticating against the endpoint, Then the API performs real JWT verification and role sync and returns 200/201.
Given an invalid or missing credential, When authenticating, Then the system returns the appropriate 400, 401, or 403 error status as defined in the DoD.
Given the implemented API fixes, When the QA test suite is executed, Then the integration tests must genuinely verify the JWT validation and role synchronization paths without mocked or stubbed success.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Authentication and role sync processing time
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Authentication success rate and QA test coverage fidelity
